overview.description: Mattis (also known as Skitgubbe in Sweden) is a unique two-phase card game popular in Scandinavia. The first phase involves collecting cards by winning tricks, while the second phase reverses the objective - players try to get rid of their collected cards by beating opponents' cards. The last player holding cards loses. It is a game of strategic timing and card management.

history.origins: The game originated in Finland as Myllymatti (mentioned in 19th century newspaper articles) and spread to Sweden where it became known as Skitgubbe. The Norwegian variant is called Mattis.
timeline: 19th Century: Myllymatti mentioned in Finnish newspapers as a popular game
Early 20th Century: Spreads to Sweden as Skitgubbe
Mid 20th Century: Norwegian variant Mattis develops with slight rule differences
Present: Played throughout Scandinavia and by Scandinavian communities abroad
history.evolution: The game's unique two-phase structure (collecting then shedding) likely evolved from combining trick-taking with beating game mechanics.
history.cultural: A popular social game in Scandinavia, often played in informal settings and family gatherings. The name 'Skitgubbe' roughly translates to 'Old Man' in Swedish.

setup.players: 3 players (standard). Can be adapted for 2 or 4 with modifications.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Ranking: A (high), K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 (low).
setup.dealing: Three cards each; remainder forms face-down stock. With three players one card remains in the stock or is set aside.

rules.objective: Avoid being the last player holding cards after both phases.
rules.gameplay: Phase one: all players play one card to each trick (from hand or stock). Suits do not matter; highest rank wins. Ties are broken by tied players playing again until one wins. After playing, each player draws from the stock to keep three cards until stock is empty. When a player has no card to play, phase one ends; players combine hand and won cards for phase two. Phase two: each turn beat the previous card or sequence, or pick up the lowest (earliest) card or sequence in the trick. Last player with cards loses.
keyRules: Phase One: Standard trick-taking, winner collects cards
Phase Two: Beat the highest card showing or pick it up
Suit ranking in Phase Two: Spades > Hearts > Diamonds > Clubs

strategy.basic: In Phase One, try to win tricks to collect high cards for Phase Two, but don't collect too many cards. In Phase Two, save your highest cards for when you really need them.
strategy.intermediate: In Phase One, control when you win tricks - winning early tricks gives you control but also more cards to shed later. Try to collect cards in strong suits (Spades and Hearts).
strategy.advanced: Card counting is crucial. Track which high cards have been played in Phase One to predict opponents' holdings in Phase Two. In Phase Two, force opponents to use their high cards early by playing medium cards that are difficult to beat without using premium cards.
tips: Don't win too many tricks in Phase One - each card won is a card you must shed in Phase Two
Save Aces and Kings of Spades for critical moments in Phase Two
Try to maintain cards in multiple suits to have flexibility in Phase Two
If you have many low cards, consider picking up early in Phase Two to consolidate your hand

difficulty.easy: Random trick play in Phase One; plays highest possible card in Phase Two without planning.
difficulty.medium: Strategic trick-taking in Phase One; saves high cards appropriately for Phase Two.
difficulty.hard: Optimal card counting; perfect timing of when to win/lose tricks in Phase One; sophisticated Phase Two hand management.

play_card.description: Phase one: play one card to the trick from hand or from the top of the stock; after playing, draw from stock to keep three cards until stock is empty. Phase two: play a card or sequence that beats the previous play, or if unable or unwilling to beat, pick up the lowest (earliest played) card or sequence in the trick.
play_card.constraints: Phase one: any card; suits do not matter; highest rank wins; ties broken by tied players playing again. Phase two: must beat with higher card or sequence in same suit, or pick up lowest in trick.

trickConfig.leadRestrictions: Suits have no significance in phase one; highest rank wins. If tie for highest, tied players play again from hand or stock until tie is broken.

validPlays.notes: Beat previous card or sequence with higher card or sequence in same suit
If cannot or do not wish to beat, must pick up the lowest (earliest played) card or sequence in the trick

edgeCases.text: Blåmattis: players with no cards at end of phase one; at first turn in phase two must pick up the lowest card on the table.
Incomplete final trick of phase one: players take back the cards they played to it and add them to hand for phase two.
Some variants: Blåmattis loses immediately. Some: tied ranks beat unique ranks in phase one.
